match.reason: The closest bank point, Translations and reflections, is a Year 7 card that covers only translations and reflection in the x-axis, while this point also needs reflection in the y-axis and rotations of 90°, 180° and 270° about the origin, which are new steps rather than small changes.

draft.title: Transformations on the Cartesian plane
card: Every point slides the same distance in the same direction. Moving right 3 and down 2 changes \((x, y)\) to \((x + 3, y - 2)\).
In the \(x\)-axis, \((x, y)\) becomes \((x, -y)\). In the \(y\)-axis, \((x, y)\) becomes \((-x, y)\).
About the origin, turning 180° changes \((x, y)\) to \((-x, -y)\). Turning 90° anticlockwise gives \((-y, x)\). Turning 270° anticlockwise gives \((y, -x)\).
Example: rotate \((3, 1)\) by 90° anticlockwise. Use \((x, y) \to (-y, x)\) to get \((-1, 3)\). A clockwise turn of 90° is the same as 270° anticlockwise.
draft.remember: Translations add to the coordinates. Reflections and rotations swap or change their signs.

a.q: The point \((4, -5)\) is reflected in the \(y\)-axis. What are its new coordinates?
a.why: A reflection in the \(y\)-axis changes the sign of \(x\) only, so \((4, -5)\) becomes \((-4, -5)\). Changing both signs, \((-4, 5)\), is a 180° rotation, not a reflection.
a.clue: The \(y\)-axis is vertical. Which coordinate stays on the same height?

b.q: Triangle vertex \(P(2, 6)\) is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of its image?
b.why: A 90° clockwise turn is the same as 270° anticlockwise, which changes \((x, y)\) to \((y, -x)\). So \((2, 6)\) becomes \((6, -2)\). The point \((-6, 2)\) comes from turning anticlockwise instead.
